authority: Owner directions in this development task

decisions.decision: threat-dynamics is a peer domain of ai-governance-regime holding threat classification and dynamic, reactive threat observability. Its specification is NIST SP 2400-102e2026 ipd (Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations, initial public draft), section 4, the agentic attack classes NISTAML.061-.067.
constraints: SP 2400-102 is an attack taxonomy, not a control framework: its identifiers name attack classes here and never governance controls.

The edition is an initial public draft (comments due 2026-12-18). Re-pin at the final edition and re-check every quoted identifier; the draft writes 'SI' where earlier editions wrote 'AI', so identifiers and section titles are quoted exactly.
Out of scope, as in SP 2400-102: traditional cybersecurity and non-adversarial inaccuracy.

decisions.decision: Observe, never decide. threat-dynamics publishes observations (CLEAR, THREAT_SUSPECTED, THREAT_CONFIRMED, the SP 2400-102 4.1.1 stage, and the red-team GATE_PASS / GATE_FAIL) and Sources; ai-governance-regime consumes them and decides. No machine here halts, revokes, permits, raises an incident or latches, and none dispatches an agent.
constraints: The two domains are coupled only through the published lanes in threat-sources.json.
Triage and response agents stay in ai-governance-regime (GOV07, GOV16).

decisions.decision: The candidate machines are 11: THR01-THR07, one detector per class NISTAML.061-.067; THR08 the red-team result gate (governance gap 3); THR09 vendor canary drift (gap 6); THR10 cross-domain exposure (gap 5); THR00 the worst-wins threat roll-up over the observers (THR08 excluded: a gate is not a live threat level).
constraints: Each detector has adversarial and benign near-miss simulations (SP 2400-102 5.1.3); every confirming and gate CES is fired by a simulation.

decisions.decision: Every input is a Source through the ISRE. Until a milestone stages its producer, each input cell is a simulated Source with SURFACE_SPEC.md Sources & Sensors semantics (create body: type simulated, region, pattern, frequency, amplitude, dcOffset), composed by the PE. The simulations in threat-sources.json are the test path; the machines' inputSequences are machine-granularity authoring fixtures and are not a substitute.
constraints: Only patterns deterministic in globalStep: binary, constant, square, linear-ramp. sine is excluded for rounding, random-walk and gaussian-noise for nondeterminism.
Each simulation resets both halves (POST {re}/api/engine/reset, POST {pe}/api/reset) before it runs.
Producers are staged per milestone (GOV-SD-14); a staged producer replaces the simulated Source for its cell, with the same region and semantics.

decisions.decision: Band [17440:17759], directly above ai-governance-regime [16960:17429]: inputs 16 cells per machine from 17440, outputs 8 per machine from 17600, the roll-up input [17680:17706] and output [17707:17709]. Code prefix THR.
constraints: Above the corpus vector budget (16944): the domain runs in the shared extension corpus with ai-governance-regime (GOV-SD-12, MACHINE_CONCEPT 9.3); the standard budget is unchanged.

decisions.decision: Admission order: threat-dynamics is admitted before ai-governance-regime, the producer before its consumer.

The semantic amendments TD-SA-01..06 are approved as proposed, with the suggested resolutions of the open review items (owner, 2026-11-25): THR08 passes at an attack success rate of 0.05 or less (TD-SA-05); a 3-step debounce confirms a continuous breach (TD-SA-02); THR09 and THR10 keep GOV16's bands (TD-SA-06); the simulated-Source sample formula is added to SURFACE_SPEC (TD-R04).
decisions.source: owner: "use your suggestions and i approve all of them"; closes TD-R03

decisions.decision: Outputs are latched. Owner, 2026-11-27: "the output is latched". On a step where a CES asserts, the engine writes the machine's whole output region with the merged vector; on a step where none asserts, the region keeps the last vector written. Observed identically on C++, LSP, Scala, Rust and Go (threat-dynamics live run 2026-11-26). An observer's level therefore means the last level it wrote, not a reading taken on the current step; the package evaluator models the latch.
